characters.name: King Shahryar
characters.description: Ruler of the sons of Sásán who, betrayed by his wife, marries and kills a new bride each morning; central narrator-frame monarch
characters.scope: STORY OF KING SHAHRYAR AND HIS BROTHER

characters.name: Shah Zaman
characters.description: Younger brother of King Shahryar, King of Samarcand; witnesses his wife's infidelity and recovers his health
characters.scope: STORY OF KING SHAHRYAR AND HIS BROTHER

characters.name: Wazir (Shahryar's minister)
characters.description: Chief minister who conveys Shahryar's invitation, executes the King's orders and brings Shahrazad to the Sultan
characters.scope: STORY OF KING SHAHRYAR AND HIS BROTHER

characters.name: the Queen
characters.description: Shahryar's wife whose infidelity triggers Shahryar's murderous vow
characters.scope: STORY OF KING SHAHRYAR AND HIS BROTHER

characters.name: Shahrazad (Shahrázád)
characters.description: Elder daughter of the Wazir who volunteers to marry the king and tells nightly tales to save other women
characters.scope: STORY OF KING SHAHRYAR AND HIS BROTHER

characters.name: Dunyazad
characters.description: Younger sister of Shahrazad who asks her to tell the nightly stories
characters.scope: STORY OF KING SHAHRYAR AND HIS BROTHER

characters.name: Merchant (Trader)
characters.description: Unnamed merchant who appears in the "Tale of the Merchant and the Jinni" and in the Bull & Ass tale; protagonist of several embedded stories
characters.scope: TALE OF THE TRADER AND THE JINNI; TALE OF THE BULL AND THE ASS

characters.name: the Ifrit / Jinni (from the pitcher)
characters.description: Supernatural being released from a sealed jar who threatens and bargains with the Fisherman and other characters
characters.scope: TALE OF THE TRADER AND THE JINNI; THE FISHERMAN AND THE JINNI

characters.name: First Shaykh (owner of the gazelle)
characters.description: Old man who tells a tale about his cousin (the gazelle) and a bewitched son
characters.scope: TALE OF THE TRADER AND THE JINNI / THE FIRST SHAYKH'S STORY

characters.name: Gazelle (the cousin)
characters.description: Woman transformed into a gazelle in the First Shaykh's story; consistently identified as the Shaykh's cousin
characters.scope: TALE OF THE TRADER AND THE JINNI / THE FIRST SHAYKH'S STORY

characters.name: Second Shaykh (owner of two greyhounds)
characters.description: Old man who tells a tale about his two brothers and the fate of their wealth
characters.scope: TALE OF THE TRADER AND THE JINNI / THE SECOND SHAYKH'S STORY

characters.name: Two greyhounds
characters.description: Dogs owned by the Second Shaykh; they feature in his recounted adventures
characters.scope: TALE OF THE TRADER AND THE JINNI / THE SECOND SHAYKH'S STORY

characters.name: Third Shaykh (owner of the mare-mule)
characters.description: Old man who tells a tale of being transformed and of his wife becoming a mule
characters.scope: TALE OF THE TRADER AND THE JINNI / THE THIRD SHAYKH'S STORY

characters.name: Mare-mule (the wife)
characters.description: Woman transformed into a she-mule in the Third Shaykh's tale
characters.scope: TALE OF THE TRADER AND THE JINNI / THE THIRD SHAYKH'S STORY

characters.name: Bull
characters.description: Speaking bull in the fable contrasted with an ass about labour and ease
characters.scope: TALE OF THE BULL AND THE ASS

characters.name: Ass
characters.description: Speaking ass in the fable who gives counsel to the Bull
characters.scope: TALE OF THE BULL AND THE ASS

characters.name: the Herdsman
characters.description: Keeper of cattle in the Bull and Ass story and in the First Shaykh's tale
characters.scope: TALE OF THE BULL AND THE ASS; THE FIRST SHAYKH'S STORY

characters.name: Herdsman's daughter
characters.description: Woman skilled in magic in the First Shaykh's story who restores the bewitched

characters.name: The Fisherman
characters.description: Poor man who hauls up a sealed pitcher and releases a Jinni; protagonist of his eponymous story

characters.name: Sulayman (Solomon)
characters.description: Prophet-king invoked in Jinn-backstory; referenced as the sealer who imprisoned the Jinni
characters.scope: THE FISHERMAN AND THE JINNI (JINN'S BACKSTORY)

characters.name: Asaf son of Barkhiyá
characters.description: Minister of Solomon who in the Jinn's backstory seizes supernatural beings
characters.scope: THE FISHERMAN AND THE JINNI (JINN'S BACKSTORY)

characters.name: Sakhr al-Jinni
characters.description: Famed jinn of Solomonic legend mentioned in the Jinni's account
characters.scope: THE FISHERMAN AND THE JINNI (JINN'S BACKSTORY)

characters.name: King Yunan
characters.description: Ruler afflicted with leprosy in the "Tale of the Wazir and the Sage Duban"
characters.scope: TALE OF THE WAZIR AND THE SAGE DUBAN

characters.name: Sage Duban
characters.description: Learned physician who cures King Yunan by a unique method and whose fate unfolds in the tale
characters.scope: TALE OF THE WAZIR AND THE SAGE DUBAN

characters.name: Wazir (of King Yunan)
characters.description: Envious minister who plots against the sage Duban in King Yunan's tale
characters.scope: TALE OF THE WAZIR AND THE SAGE DUBAN

characters.name: King Sindibad
characters.description: Monarch in the hunting tale whose falcon saves him from poisoned water

characters.name: the Falcon
characters.description: Sindibad's hawk whose action averts disaster by upsetting poisoned water

characters.name: Parrot
characters.description: Talkative parrot who tells an injured husband of his wife's infidelity in a popular folk tale

characters.name: Merchant (husband in parrot tale)
characters.description: Husband who punishes the parrot for telling of his wife's adultery

characters.name: The Prince (in "Prince and the Ogress")
characters.description: Young royal who is almost devoured by an ogress and saved by prayer

characters.name: Ghúlah (the Ogress)
characters.description: Monstrous ogress who lures the Prince and intends to devour him

characters.name: The Porter
characters.description: Porter of Baghdad who is led to a rich house and subjected to the three ladies' revels
characters.scope: THE PORTER AND THE THREE LADIES OF BAGHDAD

characters.name: Eldest Lady
characters.description: One of the three ladies of Baghdad who invites and entertains the Porter
characters.scope: THE PORTER AND THE THREE LADIES OF BAGHDAD

characters.name: Cateress (provisioner)
characters.description: One of the three ladies who provides food, perfumes and wine to guests
characters.scope: THE PORTER AND THE THREE LADIES OF BAGHDAD

characters.name: Procuratrix / Portress
characters.description: One of the three household women who admits the Porter and manages the service
characters.scope: THE PORTER AND THE THREE LADIES OF BAGHDAD

characters.name: First Kalandar
characters.description: First of the three mendicant Kalandars who tells a personal tale in the Porter's story
characters.scope: THE PORTER AND THE THREE LADIES OF BAGHDAD / FIRST KALANDAR'S TALE

characters.name: Third Kalandar
characters.description: Third mendicant who narrates a further marvellous adventure
characters.scope: THE PORTER AND THE THREE LADIES OF BAGHDAD / THIRD KALANDAR'S TALE

characters.name: Caliph Harun al-Rashid
characters.description: The historical Abbasid Caliph who appears incognito among the people and in the Porter's tale
characters.scope: THE PORTER AND THE THREE LADIES OF BAGHDAD; THE THREE APPLES

characters.name: Ja'afar
characters.description: Ja'afar al‑Barmaki, the Caliph's vizier—appears as minister/agent in multiple scenes
characters.scope: THE PORTER AND THE THREE LADIES OF BAGHDAD; THE THREE APPLES

characters.name: Masrur
characters.description: Masrur, the Caliph's eunuch/sworder who accompanies Harun on his rounds
characters.scope: THE PORTER AND THE THREE LADIES OF BAGHDAD

characters.name: Hunchback / the Gobbo
characters.description: Hunchbacked groom who is forced into marriage (mocked as a groom) and later ends up in the privy; central comic figure in the bridal episode

characters.name: Sitt al‑Husn (Lady of Beauty)
characters.description: Wazir Shams al‑Din's daughter, famed for extraordinary beauty; bride in the Hunchback episode

characters.name: Badr al‑Din Hasan
characters.description: Son of Nur al‑Din (Wazir of Bassorah), raised and later central to the "Three Apples" chain of events; also called Hasan
characters.scope: THE THREE APPLES (NUR AL‑DIN / BADR AL‑DIN STORY)

characters.name: Nur al‑Din Ali
characters.description: Wazir of Bassorah who leaves family, rises to office and dies leaving a son Hasan; father of Badr al‑Din Hasan
characters.scope: THE THREE APPLES / NUR AL‑DIN ALI STORY

characters.name: Shams al‑Din Mohammed
characters.description: Wazir of Egypt, brother of Nur al‑Din; father of Sitt al‑Husn
characters.scope: THE THREE APPLES / SHAMS AL‑DIN MOHAMMED STORY

characters.name: Wazir (of Bassorah)
characters.description: Older Wazir of Bassorah who hosts Nur al‑Din and later adopts/helps Badr al‑Din Hasan
characters.scope: THE THREE APPLES / NUR AL‑DIN ALI STORY

characters.name: the Cook (Hasan of Bassorah)
characters.description: Former rogue turned cook who adopts and raises Badr al‑Din Hasan in Damascus
characters.scope: THE THREE APPLES / BADR AL‑DIN IN DAMASCUS

characters.name: Ajib (namesake/later boy)
characters.description: Name used for the Hunchback-groom's son / later a handsome boy (several Ajibs appear in tales)
characters.scope: THE THREE APPLES / HUNCHBACK EPISODE & NUR AL‑DIN TALE

characters.name: a Jew (money-changer)
characters.description: Unnamed Jewish money-changer who buys a ship's cargo and later appears in the "Three Apples" sequence

characters.name: Ajib (boy, grandson searching)
characters.description: Young boy, grandson searching for his missing father; protagonist in family reunion episode

characters.name: Badr al-Din Hasan (Hasan the Bassorite)
characters.description: Cook from Bassorah who is later revealed to be the son of Nur al-Din and father of Ajib; poet and courtier in Cairo

characters.name: the Eunuch (Láik)
characters.description: Castrato servant and companion to Ajib; follows and attends the boy

characters.name: Ajib's grandfather
characters.description: Unidentified grandfather accompanying Ajib on the search for his father

characters.name: Mother of Badr al-Din Hasan
characters.description: Widow of Nur al-Din, mother of Badr al-Din Hasan who weeps and keeps a tomb for her missing son until reunion

characters.name: Shams al-Din (the Wazir)
characters.description: Wazir who searches for his brother's son and eventually reunites the family; uncle of Ajib

characters.name: Sitt al-Husn (the Lady of Beauty)
characters.description: Daughter of the Wazir; wife of Badr al-Din Hasan and called the Lady of Beauty

characters.name: the Sultan (of Bassorah)
characters.description: Ruler who receives the Wazir and later tests and favours Badr al-Din Hasan

characters.name: the Viceroy of Damascus
characters.description: Regional governor in Damascus who interacts with Shams al-Din over the cook's case

characters.name: the Carpenter
characters.description: Carpenter summoned by Shams al-Din to make a wooden cross for punishment

characters.name: Shahrazad (frame)
characters.description: Story-teller who narrates the Nights to the King over successive nights

characters.name: Dunyazad (frame)
characters.description: Shahrazad's sister and interlocutor in the frame narration

characters.name: the King (frame)
characters.description: Ruler listening to Shahrazad's tales (frame narrator's audience) often referred to as 'the King' or 'King of the age'

characters.name: Caliph Harun al-Rashid (mention/frame)
characters.description: Caliph referenced as hearing reports of stories via his Wazir; appears in framing commentary

characters.name: Ja'afar the Barmecide (frame mention)
characters.description: Wazir to the Caliph mentioned as teller/receiver of tales in the frame

characters.name: the Tailor
characters.description: Tailor who finds and takes the Hunchback home; central narrator of the Hunchback's Tale

characters.name: the Tailor's wife
characters.description: Wife of the Tailor who feeds the Hunchback the fatal mouthful; instigator of disposal plan

characters.name: the Hunchback (the Gobbo)
characters.description: Jester-like hunchback encountered by the Tailor and his wife who dies after choking on a fish-bone

characters.name: the black slave-girl
characters.description: Slave-girl of the Jewish physician who lets the Tailor and his wife into the physician's house and inadvertently triggers the chain of events

characters.name: the Jewish physician (the leach)
characters.description: Jewish doctor who finds the Hunchback dead in his house and passes the corpse on to avoid danger

characters.name: the Reeve (controller of the Sultan's kitchen)
characters.description: Official who finds the Hunchback in his house and believes the corpse a thief, strikes him and passes him on

aliases.text: Reeve, the controller of the Sultan's kitchen

characters.name: the Nazarene broker
characters.description: Christian (Nazarene) broker who stumbles upon the body, assaults it in drunkenness and is seized as the murderer; later narrator of his own story
characters.scope: The Hunchback's Tale; The Nazarene Broker's Story

characters.name: the watchman of the bazar
characters.description: Local market watchman who intervenes when the Nazarene and the corpse are found fighting; arrests people

characters.name: the Charley
characters.description: Public torch-bearer/watch official who ties up and brings the Nazarene before the Governor

characters.name: the Torch-bearer / executioner (hangman)
characters.description: Official who performs the hanging; later prepares to hang successive confessors

characters.name: the Governor (the Wali)
characters.description: Local governor who adjudicates the apparent murders and orders punishments

characters.name: the young merchant / youth (in the Nazarene's tale)
characters.description: Handsome youth from Baghdad who loses his right hand after an episode in Cairo and is later a companion of the Nazarene

aliases.text: a youth as handsome as could be

characters.name: Badr al-Din al-Bostáni (the Gardener)
characters.description: Merchant in Cairo who deals with the Nazarene broker and the youth; appears in the broker's account

characters.name: the Lady (mistress in Cairo)
characters.description: Wealthy lady who becomes the young merchant's lover, gives him money and later dies; unnamed mistress in the broker's tale

characters.name: the donkey-boy / ass-driver
characters.description: Minor attendant who carries the young merchant on an ass to the lady's house and later returns with him

characters.name: the Reeve (narrator)
characters.description: Controller of the Sultan's kitchen who tells his own bizarre story about a lady and cumin-ragout

characters.name: the Lady Zubaydah
characters.description: Prominent lady (Lady Zubaydah) invoked in the Reeve's Tale; her household and palace feature in the narrative

characters.name: the Jewish doctor (narrator)
characters.description: Jewish physician who later tells his own tale of Damascus, murder and hidden treasure; previously appears in the Hunchback chain

characters.name: the Tailor (later narrator)
characters.description: Tailor who tells the story of how the Hunchback circuit of blame unfolded; narrator of the Tailor's Tale

characters.name: the Barber (Al-Sámit)
characters.description: Barber who calls himself 'the Silent Man' and narrates his own life and the misfortunes of six brothers; pivotal figure in the Tailor's Tale
characters.scope: The Tailor's Tale; The Barber's Tale

characters.name: Al-Bakbúk
characters.description: Barber's eldest brother, nicknamed the prattler; one brother who became a hunchback after a tailor-and-woman episode

characters.name: Al-Haddár
characters.description: Barber's second brother, nicknamed the babbler, left paralysed in his story

characters.name: Al-Fakík
characters.description: Barber's third brother, nicknamed the gabbler, rendered blind in his episode

characters.name: Al-Kuz al-aswáni
characters.description: Barber's fourth brother, the long-necked 'Gugglet', punished and maimed in his tale

characters.name: Al-Nashshár
characters.description: Barber's fifth brother, the sawyer/seller of glass who loses his ears and gains fortune via a compassionate lady

characters.name: Shakáshik
characters.description: Barber's sixth brother, called Many-clamours, subjected to violent mutilation in his misadventures

characters.name: Al-Mustansir bi'llah
characters.description: Caliph in the Barber's anecdote who hears the Barber's story and interacts with him

characters.name: the Barmecide (Wazir)
characters.description: High minister figure referenced in multiple frame contexts (also Ja'afar in frame); appears in epilogues and patron contexts
characters.scope: Frame narrative; The Tailor's Tale references
